kicker: How small can a verifier be?

scenes.headline: How small can a model that checks answers be?
scenes.sub: Nineteen verifiers, three tasks, one H100, and a curve that switches on.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Snickers! Reasoning models practise against a verifier, an automatic check on their answers. How big must that checker be?

scenes.label: The finding
scenes.text: Verification is flat, then on: below a task-specific size a verifier sits at chance, and above it the curve barely moves.

items.say: Nineteen verifiers span almost five orders of magnitude. Eleven were pretrained from scratch, to probe below anything you can download.

items.text: Three tasks, harder and harder to check
items.say: Three tasks: Countdown and Maze can be checked exactly; faithfulness judging has only human labels.
Every rung trains on the same data and is scored on the same twelve hundred balanced examples, so chance is exactly one half.

scenes.title: Maze accuracy by verifier size
scenes.note: four tenths of a point across a 3,500x size increase
scenes.say: On Maze: zero point nine two eight at two million parameters, zero point nine three two at seven billion. Four tenths of a point, across thirty-five hundred times the size.

left.title: Chain-of-thought target
left.say: At one million parameters, trained to reason first, the model echoes the puzzle, then collapses into babble. Not one of twelve hundred outputs gives a verdict.

right.title: Verdict-only target
items: Matches the whole ladder above it
right.say: Train the same model to give only the verdict, and it matches the entire ladder above it. At this scale, chain of thought is a format cost.

steps.label: If each model failed different examples
steps.say: A flat curve has two explanations. Each model might fail a different slice of the data.

steps.label: They fail the same ones
steps.say: Or they all fail the same examples. It's this: joint failures run four point eight times above chance on Countdown, and thirteen on Maze.

scenes.text: Verifier size should be a measured parameter, not an assumed one, and measuring it is cheap.

recap: Below a task-specific size, verifiers sit at chance
Above it, the curve barely moves
Plateau models all fail the same examples
scenes.say: To recap: flat, then on; at the smallest sizes, ask for the verdict alone; and the data sets the plateau.
